 Nickeil Alexander-Walker lit up the Cavaliers with 25 points (8-of-17 FGs), three rebounds, one assist, one block and four three-pointers on Thursday.
 24 hours after NAW scored 23 points in a loss to Miami, he was able to surpass that mark in a win. His scoring had been slightly down since he dropped 31 points in the season opener, but he has been able to get back on track as of late. Outside of a drop in free throw percentage, his production has been in line with what he did during last season’s breakout. If he continues to contribute to this level, he’ll be one of the better players in fantasy basketball once again.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, one assist, one steal and five three-pointers against the Heat on Wednesday. 
 Alexander-Walker led the Hawks with 23 points, breaking a stretch of three consecutive games where he fell short of at least 20 points. He’s made at least four three-pointers in three of five games so far this season. Alexander-Walker averaged a career-high 3.2 made three-pointers per game last season and he’s carried his outside shooting success into this year.

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 31 points (8-of-15 FGs, 10-of-13 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s 132-125 victory over the Magic. 
 Alexander-Walker averaged 20.8 points in his first season with the Hawks and started his second year in Atlanta by dropping 31 on the Magic. Two of his five three-pointers came with less than two minutes left in the fourth quarter to help seal the win. Alexander-Walker is coming off his best season in the NBA and the 28-year-old guard appears to still be ascending.

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker accumulated 16 points (4-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s exhibition against the Thunder. 
 Alexander-Walker was the only Hawks starter available for Monday’s game, and he played 25 minutes. NAW is coming off the most productive season of his NBA career and won Most Improved Player honors. While capable of providing top-50 fantasy value, Alexander-Walker should come off the board just after that threshold in 12-team formats.

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker finished with 11 points (3-of-8 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), one rebound, two assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Thursday’s loss to the Knicks. 
 Alexander-Walker struggled on Thursday, as did several Hawks players. He finished with more turnovers than made field goals, and didn’t make a big impact as a facilitator or defender in his 29 minutes. The unspectacular season-ending performance was unfortunate for Alexander-Walker, who made huge strides in his first season in Atlanta. He earned the NBA’s Most Improved Player award and was a reliable contributor in fantasy leagues. His role shouldn’t change much going next season, which means he’ll likely have strong fantasy value.

 Nickeil Alexander accounted for 15 points (5-of-11 FGs), four rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers in Saturday’s Game 4 loss to the Knicks. 
 As a team, the Hawks shot 10-of-41 from beyond the arc on Saturday, and Alexander-Walker was responsible for five of the makes. While he had a good night shooting the basketball, the NBA’s Most Improved Player did not provide much value overall. And the Knicks have done a good job of defending Alexander-Walker thus far, as he’s scored 17 points or less in all four games. With the series tied at two games apiece, the teams return to New York for Game 5 on Tuesday.

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker was named the NBA’s 2025-26 Most Improved Player. 
 Alexander-Walker exploded with a career year in his first season with the Hawks. The 27-year-old shooting guard averaged 20.8 points, 1.3 steals and 3.2 three-pointers while shooting 45 percent from the field and 39 percent from behind the three-point line. Alexander-Walker set the Hawks record for three-pointers made in a season. Atlanta holds a 2-1 series lead over the Knicks heading into Saturday’s Game 4.

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker accounted for 17 points (6-of-17 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), one rebound, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in Saturday’s Game 1 loss to the Knicks. 
 Among the most improved players in the NBA this season, Alexander-Walker struggled in his Hawks postseason debut on Saturday. He shot 3-of-9 from two and wasn’t much better from beyond the arc while offering limited value in the other categories of importance. Given how well Alexander-Walker played throughout the season, nights like Saturday have not been the norm. He’ll look to improve his shooting efficiency in Game 2 on Monday.

 Aaron Wiggins provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (8-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, three assists, one block and four three-pointers on Thursday against the Cavaliers.
 Wiggins continued to shine off the bench for Atlanta. He has scored in double figures in every game this season, and after being held to just 10 points in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat, he responded with a new season high for scoring in this one. He has been excellent in fantasy basketball thus far, mostly because he is averaging 3.0 triples per game and has hit at least two shots from beyond the arc in every game this season.

 Onyeka Okongwu led the Hawks with 29 points (11-of-17 FGs), 12 rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in a 114-111 win over the Cavaliers on Thursday.
 It has been a rough start to the year for Okongwu, but he was finally able to get things going in this game. Entering this game, his season high for scoring was 11 points, and he hadn’t recorded a double-double yet. This was by far his best performance of the year and hopefully a sign of things to come. He’ll look to keep it going against the Pelicans on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Sam Merrill provided a boost off the bench with 16 points (6-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Hawks on Thursday.
 Merrill is a nice shooting option to have off the bench, but he hasn’t been as productive this year as he was last season, when he averaged 3.0 triples per game. This was the first time he surprised two threes in a game this year, which resulted in his first double-digit scoring performance. He’ll have some big nights, but his upside will be capped as a reserve. Barring an injury to a starter, he won’t be a consistent producer in fantasy basketball this year.

 James Harden led the Cavaliers with 24 points (7-of-14 FGs), five rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in a 114-111 loss to the Hawks on Thursday.
 Harden has been underwhelming this season, with his scoring, assists and shooting efficiency all down. However, he was able to get his shot going in this one, and he ended up scoring at least 20 points for the first time this season while also having his best field goal percentage of the season. However, the trade-off was a new season low for assists. Harden should be better as the season progresses, but he may not play to his third-round ADP.
 -  Noah Rubin
